page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is a large-scale, general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor architecture. It provides 180 dedicated vCPUs spanning 90 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 720 GB of system memory at a consistent 4 GB per vCPU ratio. The configuration includes per-core cache hierarchies of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for vector extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent disk operations.

Benchmark evaluations place this machine type in the upper percentiles for parallel computing and throughput. It achieves top-tier results in multi-core compute tests, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 22069, a PassMark CPU score of 123447.51, and high clang compilation throughput. Memory performance demonstrates cached read bandwidth reaching 13454.22 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth exceeding 356 GB/sec. In distributed data and memory stress environments, the platform delivers 211.43 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations, alongside strong performance across CPU-based large language model inference workloads.

The primary tradeoff of the c3d-standard-180 is its reliance on networked disk volumes, meaning I/O-bound tasks must factor in network storage bandwidth rather than ultra-low-latency local NVMe drives. However, its high resource density eliminates virtualization overhead across fragmented smaller nodes, yielding high qualitative cost efficiency for scaled workloads. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation, enterprise application backends, large in-memory databases, data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving tiers.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-180 is an x86_64 general-purpose compute instance equipped with 180 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor and 720 GB of system memory. Operating at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration features AVX-512 instruction support, hardware cryptography, and substantial multi-level CPU caching. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, depending on network-attached storage for persistent workloads. In synthetic and application-level benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing capability, reaching top-decile scores in Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and Redis memory operations processing over 211 million operations per second. While lacking high-speed local NVMe disks, its massive parallel execution footprint and high memory bandwidth provide efficient execution for resource-intensive enterprise backends, large in-memory databases, batch data engineering jobs, and high-concurrency web services.
